summary: Independent review of Jin shu 53 (愍懷太子). Year-level Hui-era conversions that stay inside their lunar year are supported: 惠帝即位 AD 290; 元康元年 AD 291; 九年六月 AD 299; 永康元年 months 1/3/6 AD 300; 永甯/永寧元年 AD 301; 太安元年三月 / 太安初 AD 302. The main Western-year defect is 元康九年十二月, whose concordance month begins 8 Jan AD 300 (annals 十二月壬戌), so deposition, trial, 考竟 deaths, and the AD 299 hints built from them are incorrect. Childhood 武帝愛之 and 太子時年五歲 are undated attestations, not unresolved years or a 266–290 Wu-reign window; 23 sui at death must not be inverted into a birth year. Invented 元康中 291–299 intervals, exact AD 290 for undated Guangling/tutor scenes, and filiation-only 291 father claims are unsupported. Later comparisons (宣帝, 楊氏故事, 申生/孝己, 楚建/戾園, 史臣曰) and 太安初 追諡 are reception, not living activity. Princess Changguang’s words are a forgery. Lady of Yicheng’s death and Bin’s birth are attested without years. Competing annal days (六月壬寅 vs 己卯; 五月己巳 vs 四月) are preserved without choosing a winner. Hints must be rebuilt from the surviving personal events.
